editorial:
Imagine you have a perfect life as a successful businessman, and then one split-second mistake behind the wheel ruins everything. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a man who causes a fatal car crash, which puts him right in the crosshairs of the press. Instead of just reporting on the accident, the newspapers start digging into his old secrets from World War II. It creates a heavy, tense mood as you watch him struggle with the gap between who he is now and who he was back then in Greece. You feel the pressure building as his polished world starts to crack open.

The acting is really solid and makes the guilt feel real. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the way the story jumps between the present and the past keeps you curious about the truth. If you like stories about secrets and moral dilemmas, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you should try to find a high-quality version to appreciate the scenery. I suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture, or you can try renting it on Apple TV if you want a quick watch.
endingExplained: In the end, the man cannot run away from his history. The investigation reveals the terrible things he did during the war, stripping away his fake image of being a good person. He realizes that no matter how much money or power he has now, he is still responsible for his past crimes. He ends up broken and defeated, showing that the truth always comes out eventually, even decades later.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and character studies.
